terms.shortDefinition: A dedicated secondary UI pane rendered when Claude generates substantial (>15 lines), self-contained content intended to be modified, shared, or executed independently of the chat thread.
terms.officialExamTopic: Organize and curate information for optimal outputs; select appropriate output formats (artifacts for code/documents, inline for conversational responses)

keyExamTrap.myth: Artifacts should be triggered for any short code snippet or explanatory text block.
keyExamTrap.reality: Artifacts are reserved for self-contained, high-value assets (>15 lines) meant for standalone reuse (e.g., SVG, React code, complete docs). Short snippets stay inline.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Look for questions asking where a 3-line terminal command vs a 200-line React component should render.

video16sBlueprint.hook: Why does Claude put some code in a side window and some directly in chat?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: That side window is an Artifact! Reserved for standalone, reusable code, SVGs, or documents over 15 lines long.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Conversational replies and quick 3-line snippets always stay inline to avoid cluttering your workspace.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Exam Tip: Candidates failed this at 0%! Remember: standalone and reusable equals Artifact, quick explanation equals inline!

terms.shortDefinition: The prompting method of breaking down a large, multifaceted problem into sequential sub-tasks, minimizing cognitive overload and intermediate error propagation.
terms.officialExamTopic: Apply task decomposition techniques to structure complex requests

keyExamTrap.myth: Providing a single mega-prompt with 10 complex requirements is faster and equally accurate.
keyExamTrap.reality: Decomposed prompts allow Claude to verify intermediate outputs, dramatically reducing compounding hallucinations.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Scenarios involving multi-step audits, legal contract comparisons, or multi-tier code refactoring.

video16sBlueprint.hook: Why does Claude hallucinate when you ask it to do three complex jobs at once?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: LLMs suffer from cognitive overload when solving chained logic in a single shot without intermediate tokens.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Task decomposition forces Claude to execute Step 1, verify the intermediate state, then proceed to Step 2.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Exam Tip: For multi-step enterprise workflows, always decompose complex instructions into numbered sequential stages!

terms.shortDefinition: Anthropic's recommended structural syntax for delineating instructions, context documents, examples, and output constraints within prompts using clean semantic tags.
terms.officialExamTopic: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks

keyExamTrap.myth: Markdown headers (# or ##) provide the same parsing precision to Claude as XML tags.
keyExamTrap.reality: Claude is fine-tuned specifically on XML tags (<context>, <instructions>, <rules>), eliminating ambiguity between data and instructions.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Prompts containing user-supplied untrusted input that could cause prompt injection.

video16sBlueprint.hook: What is Anthropic's secret weapon for structuring complex prompts?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: XML tags! Wrapping sections in tags like <context> and <instructions> gives Claude mathematical clarity on where data ends and commands begin.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: This prevents prompt injection and stops Claude from confusing your example data with actual user instructions.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Anthropic Associate Exam Gold: Always use semantic XML tags to wrap input documents and reference criteria!

terms.officialExamTopic: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks

keyExamTrap.myth: System prompts are just normal user messages prepended to the chat history.
keyExamTrap.reality: In Anthropic's API, system is a top-level parameter with higher behavioral adherence and persistent role conditioning.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Architecture questions asking where to define persistent guardrails across a 50-turn conversation.

client.messages.create(
  model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",

)

video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Even across 50 multi-turn conversation exchanges, the system prompt retains maximum steering priority.

terms.term: Claude Model Family (Haiku vs Sonnet vs Opus)
terms.shortDefinition: Anthropic's three-tier model hierarchy balancing speed, cost, and reasoning depth: Haiku (fast/low-cost), Sonnet (balanced enterprise workhorse), Opus (deep complex reasoning).
terms.officialExamTopic: Differentiate between Claude model types (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) and align model selection with task requirements

keyExamTrap.myth: Opus is always the recommended model for production applications because it is the largest.
keyExamTrap.reality: Sonnet 3.5 frequently outperforms older Opus on coding and tool use at 1/5th the cost and significantly higher velocity.
keyExamTrap.examClue: High-volume classification vs real-time coding vs edge low-latency batch processing.

video16sBlueprint.hook: Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus: Which Claude model should you deploy in production?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: Haiku delivers near-instant speed at minimal cost for classification and routing.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Sonnet 3.5 is the enterprise workhorse with frontier coding and vision, while Opus tackles the deepest multi-step research.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Exam Question Alert: Never default to the largest model! Always match volume, latency SLA, and token cost to the tier!

terms.shortDefinition: Claude's capacity to process up to 200,000 tokens (~150,000 words) in a single request, requiring deliberate memory hygiene to avoid latency inflation and attention dispersion.
terms.officialExamTopic: Understand and manage context limitations/memory: when to restart, summarize, or persist

keyExamTrap.myth: Because the window is 200k tokens, you should leave entire conversation threads running indefinitely.
keyExamTrap.reality: Degraded latency, higher per-turn cost, and 'needle-in-a-haystack' retrieval noise make resetting or summarizing sessions necessary.
keyExamTrap.examClue: When to clear context, summarize previous turns, or spin up a new session.

video16sBlueprint.hook: Claude can handle 200,000 tokens—so should you ever reset the chat?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: Yes! Just because Claude can read 500 pages doesn't mean your budget and latency want to pay for 500 pages on every turn.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Long contexts increase time-to-first-token and cost. Pruning and summarizing keeps responses sharp.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Associate Exam Rule: When a conversation shifts topics, restart or summarize rather than dragging the entire historical context!

terms.shortDefinition: An Anthropic API feature allowing developers to cache large static prompt prefixes (codebases, documentation, system prompts) for up to 5 minutes, slashing cost by 90% and latency by 85%.
terms.officialExamTopic: Optimize token usage, latency, and cost-performance trade-offs

keyExamTrap.myth: Prompt caching is automatically applied to any message sent to the API.
keyExamTrap.reality: Developers must explicitly declare cache breakpoints using the 'cache_control': {'type': 'ephemeral'} parameter on content blocks over 1,024 tokens.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Scenarios involving large book analyses, customer service agent repos, or recurring system rules.

video16sBlueprint.hook: How do you slash your Claude API costs by 90% in large context applications?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: Prompt Caching! Set an ephemeral cache breakpoint on your static documents or huge system prompts.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Subsequent API calls read from memory instead of recalculating, reducing latency by up to 85%.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Exam Tip: Minimum cacheable prompt size is 1,024 tokens. Look for 'cache_control: ephemeral' on the exam!

terms.shortDefinition: The API return state when Claude decides that answering the user's prompt requires executing an external function, returning structured JSON arguments and stop_reason='tool_use'.
terms.officialExamTopic: Select appropriate Claude product features and understand programmatic tool execution

keyExamTrap.myth: Claude directly invokes your internal database or executes code on your server.
keyExamTrap.reality: Claude never executes client-side code; it outputs the JSON arguments and pauses with stop_reason='tool_use', waiting for the client to run the tool and return the result.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Who executes the code when tool_use is invoked, and what does the client pass back?

video16sBlueprint.hook: Does Claude actually run the tools you give it in the API?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: No! Claude does NOT execute code on your server. It returns a stop_reason called 'tool_use' with structured JSON parameters.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Your client application executes the database query or API, then feeds the result back to Claude.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Certification Golden Rule: Claude decides WHEN to call and outputs parameters; your client application does the actual execution!

terms.shortDefinition: Anthropic's open standard for securely connecting AI assistants to local or remote data sources, enterprise tools, and execution environments via standardized client-host-server architectures.

keyExamTrap.myth: MCP is a proprietary proprietary closed API for Claude Desktop only.
keyExamTrap.reality: MCP is an open protocol with open-source SDKs (TypeScript, Python) allowing any agent to connect to standardized resource and tool servers.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Standardized tool integration across multiple tools without bespoke point-to-point wrappers.

terms.shortDefinition: Instructing Claude to 'think step-by-step' or articulate reasoning inside thinking tags (<thinking>...</thinking>) prior to generating the final answer.
terms.officialExamTopic: Apply prompt engineering techniques (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought)

keyExamTrap.myth: CoT is just stylistic verbosity and does not affect mathematical or logic accuracy.
keyExamTrap.reality: Generating intermediate reasoning tokens fundamentally changes the auto-regressive probability distribution, dramatically reducing logic errors.
keyExamTrap.examClue: Math problems, policy interpretations, or complex entity matching tasks.

video16sBlueprint.hook: Why do thinking tags make Claude dramatically smarter at logic problems?
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart1: Chain-of-Thought prompts give the model token workspace to compute intermediate states before committing to a final answer.
video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Asking Claude to think inside <thinking> tags decouples internal scratchpad reasoning from the polished output.
video16sBlueprint.ctaExamTip: Certification Tip: Use Chain-of-Thought whenever tasks require multi-step math, policy verification, or complex deduction!

video16sBlueprint.conceptPart2: Implement exponential backoff with jitter to pause and retry progressively without overwhelming the gateway.
